claim.quote: The T2K experiment has observed electron neutrino appearance in a muon neutrino beam produced 295 km from the Super-Kamiokande detector with a peak energy of 0.6 GeV. A total of 28 electron neutrino events were detected with an energy distribution consistent with an appearance signal, corresponding to a significance of 7.3σ when compared to 4.92 ± 0.55 expected background events.

date.note: arXiv submission November 2013; published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 112, 061802 (2014).

key_value_text.quote: a best-fit value of sin² 2θ₁₃ = 0.140⁺⁰·⁰³⁸₂₀.₀₃₂ (0.170⁺⁰·⁰⁴⁵₂₀.₀₃₇) is obtained at δ_CP=0
key_value_text.value: Best-fit sin^2(2 theta_13) = 0.140(+0.038/-0.032) for normal mass ordering (0.170(+0.045/-0.037) for inverted), at delta_CP = 0.

name: T2K observation of electron-neutrino appearance

summary.plain: In 2014, T2K confirmed for certain that muon neutrinos really do turn into electron neutrinos as they cross Japan: 28 electron-neutrino events were seen where only about 5 were expected if nothing changed, far too many to be a fluke.
summary.technical: 28 nu_e candidate events at Super-Kamiokande vs. 4.92+/-0.55 expected background; 7.3 sigma significance. Best-fit sin^2(2 theta_13)=0.140(+0.038/-0.032) (normal ordering) at delta_CP=0, combined with reactor theta_13 measurements to begin constraining delta_CP.

title: Observation of Electron Neutrino Appearance in a Muon Neutrino Beam
why_it_matters: The first observation (as opposed to indication) of muon-to-electron neutrino appearance at an accelerator, confirming that theta_13 is sizeable and opening the direct search for leptonic CP violation that culminated in T2K's 2020 delta_CP constraint.
